expected_symptom: Running dxr -E InitArgs -remove-unused-globals on the reporter shader emits struct Parent with the member Child MultipleChildren[2] but no struct Child definition, so the rewritten source no longer compiles; the same shader with a non-array member Child SingleChild keeps the definition.
godbolt_skip: Compiler Explorer runs the dxc driver, which cannot reach the rewriter at all: dxc rejects -remove-unused-globals with 'Unknown argument' (measured, variant-dxc-rejects-rewriter-flag-main-debug.txt), and CE ships no dxr. A pane could only show the rewriter's already-broken OUTPUT failing on an undefined type, which demonstrates nothing a reader could not guess and hides that DXC itself produced that source. Clang has no HLSL rewriter either, so a Clang pane adds nothing.
summary: dxr -E InitArgs -remove-unused-globals deletes struct Child even though struct Parent declares Child MultipleChildren[2]; the emitted source then fails to compile with "unknown type name Child". Reproduces on main 1.9.0.5433 (13730886e) and on all 19 stable releases v1.5.2010..v1.9.2607 that can express the option; v1.4.1907 has no rewriter options at all (invalid probe), so there is no regression window. The non-array form Child SingleChild is unaffected, and the rewriter own accounting under -no-warnings confirms the decision: //found 1 types to remove vs //found 0. The 2022-08-15 comment about unused function parameters also reproduces (agent-constructed shader). One root cause in dxcrewriteunused.cpp: type liveness is computed from value references only, so fieldDecl->getType()->getAsTagDecl() returns null for an array member and FunctionDecl::params() is never visited. Real, unfixed, no linked PR; keep open and add the rewriter label.
title: Rewriter incorrectly removes types that are used in a member array of another struct
